title: vLLM v0.9.2 startup time with and without persisted JIT caches, and CuteAFD's for comparison
question: How much does persisting the TileLang, Triton, TorchInductor and CUDA JIT caches shorten the startup of tpurtell's vLLM fork v0.9.2 on this setup?
engines: tpurtell vLLM fork v0.9.2 (vLLM build v0.1.dev20051+g487ecf187 in the logs; image digest not stated in this run)
CuteAFD v3.0.1 (comparison figure only; no receipt in this folder)
checkpoints: wrldsuksgo2mars/GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3-K3.25-v1 @ 0490d2f7 (snapshot path in the server logs), drafter snapshot bf582e4e
hardware: not stated in this run's files

goals.question: With the JIT cache directories pointed into the already persisted cache mount, how long does a warm start of the vLLM fork v0.9.2 take to ready, against a start with the caches not persisted?
goals.added_source: RUN.json protocol ('outside the frozen protocol: startup timing from the server logs (measure.sh)'); README.md:3-6

design.instrument: time from container start to the 'startup warmup complete' log line, read from docker logs -t by measure.sh
arms: vLLM v0.9.2, JIT caches not persisted (run0)
vLLM v0.9.2, JIT caches persisted, warm (run2)
design.items: one container start per arm; the only change is the four cache variables in the stack's env overlay
design.n: 2 starts (plus the populate start, goal POPULATE)

goals.headline: One start per arm (descriptive), vLLM fork v0.9.2 with K3.25-v1: ready 697 s with the JIT caches not persisted and 382 s with them persisted and warm (−45%). TileLang JIT compiles fall from 49 (222 s) to 0; CUDA graph capture 153 s against 43 s (58 s phase); weight loading is about the same (135.7 s and 139.3 s).

goals.question: How long does the first start after the change, which fills the caches, take?

arms: vLLM v0.9.2, first start after persisting the caches (run1)

goals.headline: One start: the first start after persisting the caches took 714 s to ready (48 TileLang compiles, graph capture 151 s); the run reads later starts as warm.

goals.question: Where does the vLLM fork's startup time go, phase by phase, with and without persisted caches, and how large are the persisted caches?

design.instrument: phase boundaries from the server log (weights loaded, TileLang compile begin/end, graph capture, warm-up); cache directory sizes with du

goals.headline: Not persisted: process start and weight loading 242 s, TileLang JIT 222 s (49 compiles), CUDA graph capture 153 s, warm-up ~73 s. Persisted, warm: 254 s, 0 compiles, 58 s graph-capture phase, ~64 s warm-up. Persisted cache sizes: TileLang 11 MB, Triton 88 MB, TorchInductor 6.1 MB. RESULTS.md reads the remaining time as mostly weight loading (~137 GB at about 1 GB/s plus loader overhead); this is stated, not separately measured.

goals.question: For comparison, how long does CuteAFD v3.0.1 take to ready on this setup?

design.instrument: start to ready (as stated in RESULTS.md and startup.json)
design.items: one start; checkpoint not stated in this run

goals.status_note: No CuteAFD log or receipt is published in this folder; the figure is stated in RESULTS.md and startup.json only.
goals.headline: CuteAFD v3.0.1 is stated as ready in 89 s (AOT kernels; experts loaded in 30.6 s), one start, no receipt in this folder.
